messages:
maya: quick alert — post-rollout of nvidia-device-plugin 0.9.2 in eu-west (rolled ~12h ago) we're seeing a surge of GPU pods stuck in ContainerCreating. Scheduler reports they were bound but kubelet later fails to allocate devices. Noticed queueing on the inference queue and some Dedicated customers saw increased tail latency. :eyes:

maya: sample failure from a pod: `Error: failed to start container "ml-worker": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to allocate device: device not found`

tom: can you paste `kubectl get nodes -l cluster=eu-west -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu}
{end}'` output? also any daemonset logs?

maya: output on a few nodes:
```
ip-10-0-4-12:0
ip-10-0-5-33:0
ip-10-0-6-77:4
ip-10-0-7-04:4
```
so some nodes report 0 allocatable after the rollout.

raj: seeing this in device-plugin logs on ip-10-0-4-12: `E0412 08:04:12.123456 1 plugin.go:184] advertise: advertising before driver probe, skipping GPU advertise` — basically plugin is advertising before the kernel driver finishes binding. Looks like the new plugin starts earlier in the boot/reconcile loop and races with dkms/module probe when CUDA/kernel combo isn't exactly the same.

raj: also pulled node dmesg — there are `nvidia: probe failed - version mismatch` entries. driver on host shows `525.85` but device-plugin expects the probe path that shows `525.60` (minor variant). Combined with kubelet restart window it's flaky.

sarah: recommended immediate mitigation: cordon + drain the nodes that show 0 GPUs (don't evict Dedicated customer pods if possible), scale up other healthy GPU nodes (eu-west spare pool), and rollback device-plugin to 0.9.1 while we triage.

maya: +1. I'm cordoning ip-10-0-4-12 and ip-10-0-5-33 now. leaving ip-10-0-6-77/7-04 for active traffic.

ops-bot: automation note — autoscaler policy triggered: creating 2 spot-gpu instances in eu-west-1a to compensate. ETA ~4m.

tom: for rollback: `kubectl -n kube-system set image daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin nvidia-device-plugin=redwood/nvidia-device-plugin:0.9.1` — do we want a canary first? maybe roll to one AZ then expand.

deploy-bot: rolling back ds kube-system/nvidia-device-plugin -> tag 0.9.1. Canary: eu-west-1b nodes only. Monitor `allocatable` and `pod status`.

raj: long-term we should change daemonset to probe driver readiness before advertising, e.g. wrapper that checks `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name` or `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` and waits up to Xs, plus stronger kernel module validation. Filed infra-2467.

sarah: also opened a watch to verify Dedicated SLAs in eu-west — outreach queued to impacted customers. ops team to confirm cost impact if we keep spare pool running.

maya: after rollback canary (1 AZ) allocatable recovered on canary nodes. doing full rollback now. will post final numbers in ~10m. :thumbsup: 

tom: follow-up checklist: 1) patch device-plugin to wait for driver binding 2) add node metric alert for sudden GPU allocatable=0 3) include driver/version gating in rollout job 4) postmortem in eng-infra.

maya: agreed, assigning follow-ups: raj -> plugin probe change, sarah -> customer comms & cost calc, tom -> rollout job gating. meeting at 14:30 to go over postmortem draft.

deploy-bot: rollback complete across eu-west, all nodes show expected allocatable. closing incident when metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
